key_insight: Generative approaches (including diffusion models) for offline multi-objective optimization can achieve high hypervolume yet systematically fail on other Pareto-quality metrics (e.g., generational distance) because of a distributional mismatch between the dataset frontier and the true Pareto frontier — the "offline-frontier shift."
problem_solved: Diagnoses why state-of-the-art generative MOO methods sometimes produce misleadingly good aggregate scores (hypervolume) while delivering poor proximity and diversity relative to the true Pareto front when only a finite static dataset is available.
method: Empirical comparison of generative models (diffusion and related) against evolutionary baselines across multiple MOO metrics (hypervolume, generational distance, etc.).

Formalize and illustrate the "offline-frontier shift": the distributional gap between the dataset's observed frontier and the true Pareto frontier that generative methods tend to reproduce rather than extrapolate beyond.
Metric-driven diagnosis to reveal failure modes and characterize when and why generative methods underperform on Pareto-quality metrics despite high hypervolume.
impact: Helps practitioners choose and evaluate offline MOO algorithms more robustly by exposing a key distributional failure mode; encourages multi-metric evaluation and cautious use of generative models when dataset frontiers differ from true optima.
visual_elements: Scatter plot comparing solutions from generative vs evolutionary methods colored by metric (hypervolume vs generational distance).
Schematic diagram of the offline-frontier shift: dataset frontier vs true Pareto frontier showing distributional gap and model replication of the dataset frontier.
Bar/line chart showing performance across multiple MOO metrics (hypervolume, generational distance, coverage) for each method.
Flowchart of the evaluation/diagnostic pipeline: dataset → model training → multi-metric evaluation → offline-frontier shift detection.
paper_title: The Offline-Frontier Shift: Diagnosing Distributional Limits in Generative Multi-Objective Optimization
paper_authors: Stephanie Holly, Alexandru-Ciprian Zăvoianu, Siegfried Silber, Sepp Hochreiter, Werner Zellinger
